title: Find the biggest files
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: A ranked list of the largest single files (files only, biggest first) exists: missing
The list covers files anywhere under the scanned folder or drive, not only the top level: partial
Each listed file shows where it is (its location): partial
The list is shown to the person: missing

Should the list rank by space actually taken on disk (the design's default, with both sizes shown) or by logical size? A person looking for 'the biggest files' may expect logical size, and it would put OneDrive online-only files near the top. The slice text did not settle it. Changing it swaps the heap key and the header text.

On C:\, pagefile.sys (20 GiB in the spike), hiberfil.sys (about 12.5 GiB) and swapfile.sys will lead the list. Should they be shown unlabelled (the design's default, since the spike measured them as correct), labelled as system files, or left out?
No one contested any of these: one proposal, no rival. Ranking basis (on-disk versus logical) is also an open question above.
A fixed top 100 in an App constant versus a threshold or a person-set count.
Full path in one wrapping column versus separate name and folder columns, which would need a name accessor nobody has confirmed.
The list as a section inside the outcome panel above the unreadable list versus its own expander or tab.
Computing on the UI thread inside ShowOutcome versus Task.Run from the start. The report's largestFilesMs is meant to settle this with a number.
LargestFiles under a new Core/Analysis folder, with the rule scoped to it, versus a flat Core folder.
One architecture rule with two patterns, versus none (the proposal's choice) or two separate rules.

drift: Nothing departs from the design undeclared. I checked the declared departures against the tree and they are all there as described. (1) Layout: LargestFilesPanel is the DockPanel fill child, not a Li…

drift: The design text still says index order is 'multithreaded' and that a Cancelled-scan test 'settles' the writer invariant. The code and the M1/m3 dispositions correct both (LargestFiles.cs:12-14, 21-22…

not reached: Paths of the real C:\ list's 100 rows: the report carries no paths by design (Q-016), so only row 0's size and the row count were compared with an independent reference. The other 99 rows and their shown locations were not read.

not reached: No person looked at the window. How wrapped 400-character paths, a lone-surrogate name, and the 'On disk'/'Size' columns look was judged only from report metrics (inView, heights, realized rows).

not reached: Criterion 14's probe shapes on a real list: whether an online-only OneDrive placeholder, a probe-failed system file or an open-and-growing file appears with correct values as a row. I did not open the person's OneDrive folder.
not reached: The contents of the 664 unreadable folders on C:\: the list cannot include them, and read-denied-folders returns counts only, so it could not say whether a larger file is hidden there.
not reached: Windows 10, other DPI settings, and window sizes other than the default 880x600; only Windows 11 build 26200 was exercised.
not reached: Drives other than NTFS C:\ (exFAT/FAT removable, mapped SMB share) with the list shown.
not reached: Why the independent .NET walk counted about 1.04M fewer files than the scanner (2,544,046 vs 3,580,356). It did not affect the row-0 comparison, and it is not this slice's code.
criterion not met: 11. fit the list into the outcome panel: 100 rows, a surrogate row, with the unreadable-folders list also filled
